raw: CHAPTER VI. The Shoemaker
en: [Chapter 6] The Shoemaker

raw: “Good day!” said Monsieur Defarge, looking down at the white head that bent low over the shoemaking.
en: "Good day!" said Monsieur Defarge, looking down at the white head that was bent low over his shoemaking.

raw: It was raised for a moment, and a very faint voice responded to the salutation, as if it were at a distance:
en: The head was raised for a moment, and a very faint voice responded to the greeting, sounding as if it came from far away:

raw: “Good day!”
en: "Good day!"

raw: “You are still hard at work, I see?”
en: "You are still working hard, I see?"

raw: After a long silence, the head was lifted for another moment, and the voice replied, “Yes--I am working.” This time, a pair of haggard eyes had looked at the questioner, before the face had dropped again.
en: After a long silence, the head was lifted for another moment. The voice replied, "Yes, I am working." This time, a pair of exhausted, hollow eyes looked at the questioner. Then the face dropped down again.

raw: The faintness of the voice was pitiable and dreadful.
en: The weakness of the voice was pitiful and sad.

raw: It was not the faintness of physical weakness, though confinement and hard fare no doubt had their part in it.
en: It was not the weakness of physical illness, though being locked away and eating bad food had certainly played a part.

raw: Its deplorable peculiarity was, that it was the faintness of solitude and disuse.
en: Its most tragic feature was that it was the weakness of long loneliness and lack of use.

raw: It was like the last feeble echo of a sound made long and long ago.
en: It sounded like the last faint echo of a sound made a very long time ago.

raw: So entirely had it lost the life and resonance of the human voice, that it affected the senses like a once beautiful colour faded away into a poor weak stain.
en: It had so completely lost the life and fullness of a normal human voice that listening to it felt like looking at a once beautiful color that had faded into a dull, weak stain.

raw: So sunken and suppressed it was, that it was like a voice underground.
en: It was so low and muffled that it sounded like a voice coming from deep underground.

raw: So expressive it was, of a hopeless and lost creature, that a famished traveller, wearied out by lonely wandering in a wilderness, would have remembered home and friends in such a tone before lying down to die.
en: The voice expressed a sense of a lost and hopeless soul. A starving traveler, wandering alone in a desert, would have heard that tone and remembered home and friends, just before lying down to die.

raw: Some minutes of silent work had passed: and the haggard eyes had looked up again: not with any interest or curiosity, but with a dull mechanical perception, beforehand, that the spot where the only visitor they were aware of had stood, was not yet empty.
en: A few minutes of silent work passed, and the exhausted eyes looked up again. They showed no interest or curiosity, but only a dull, automatic awareness that the spot where his visitor stood was not yet empty.

raw: “I want,” said Defarge, who had not removed his gaze from the shoemaker, “to let in a little more light here.
en: "I want," said Defarge, who had not stopped looking at the shoemaker, "to let a little more light in here.

raw: You can bear a little more?”
en: Can you handle a little more?"

raw: The shoemaker stopped his work; looked with a vacant air of listening, at the floor on one side of him; then similarly, at the floor on the other side of him; then, upward at the speaker.
en: The shoemaker stopped his work. He looked blankly at the floor on one side, as if listening. Then he looked the same way at the floor on the other side. Finally, he looked up at the speaker.

raw: “What did you say?”
en: "What did you say?"

raw: “You can bear a little more light?”
en: "Can you handle a little more light?"

raw: “I must bear it, if you let it in.” (Laying the palest shadow of a stress upon the second word.)
en: "I must handle it, if you let it in." He put the faintest hint of emphasis on the second word.

raw: The opened half-door was opened a little further, and secured at that angle for the time.
en: The wooden half-door was opened a little wider and held in place.

raw: A broad ray of light fell into the garret, and showed the workman with an unfinished shoe upon his lap, pausing in his labour.
en: A wide beam of light shone into the attic room, showing the worker pausing with an unfinished shoe on his lap.

raw: His few common tools and various scraps of leather were at his feet and on his bench.
en: His few simple tools and scraps of leather lay at his feet and on his workbench.

raw: He had a white beard, raggedly cut, but not very long, a hollow face, and exceedingly bright eyes.
en: He had a messy white beard that was not very long, a hollow face, and extremely bright eyes.

raw: The hollowness and thinness of his face would have caused them to look large, under his yet dark eyebrows and his confused white hair, though they had been really otherwise; but, they were naturally large, and looked unnaturally so.
en: The thinness of his face made his eyes look huge under his dark eyebrows and messy white hair, even though they were already naturally large, making them look unnaturally big now.

raw: His yellow rags of shirt lay open at the throat, and showed his body to be withered and worn.
en: His yellow, ragged shirt was open at the neck, showing his thin, worn-out body.

raw: He, and his old canvas frock, and his loose stockings, and all his poor tatters of clothes, had, in a long seclusion from direct light and air, faded down to such a dull uniformity of parchment-yellow, that it would have been hard to say which was which.
en: He, his old canvas jacket, his loose stockings, and all his ragged clothes had faded from being locked away from light and fresh air for so long. Everything had turned the same dull, paper-yellow color, so that it was hard to tell his clothes and his skin apart.

raw: He had put up a hand between his eyes and the light, and the very bones of it seemed transparent.
en: He held up a hand to shield his eyes from the light, and the bones inside it looked almost transparent.

raw: So he sat, with a steadfastly vacant gaze, pausing in his work.
en: He sat there, staring blankly, pausing in his work.

raw: He never looked at the figure before him, without first looking down on this side of himself, then on that, as if he had lost the habit of associating place with sound; he never spoke, without first wandering in this manner, and forgetting to speak.
en: He never looked at the person standing in front of him without first looking down to one side, then the other. It was as if he had forgotten how to connect sounds with the direction they came from. He never spoke without looking around in this confused way first. Sometimes he forgot to speak at all.

raw: “Are you going to finish that pair of shoes to-day?” asked Defarge, motioning to Mr.
en: "Are you going to finish that pair of shoes today?" asked Defarge, signaling for Mr.

raw: Lorry to come forward.
en: Lorry to step forward.

raw: “What did you say?”
en: "What did you say?"

raw: “Do you mean to finish that pair of shoes to-day?”
en: "Do you plan to finish that pair of shoes today?"

raw: “I can’t say that I mean to.
en: "I can't say that I plan to.

raw: I suppose so.
en: I suppose so.

raw: I don’t know.”
en: I don't know."

raw: But, the question reminded him of his work, and he bent over it again.
en: But the question reminded him of his work, and he bent over it again.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.

raw: Lorry came silently forward, leaving the daughter by the door.
en: Lorry walked forward quietly, leaving Lucie by the door.

raw: When he had stood, for a minute or two, by the side of Defarge, the shoemaker looked up.
en: After he stood next to Defarge for a minute or two, the shoemaker looked up.

raw: He showed no surprise at seeing another figure, but the unsteady fingers of one of his hands strayed to his lips as he looked at it (his lips and his nails were of the same pale lead-colour), and then the hand dropped to his work, and he once more bent over the shoe.
en: He did not seem surprised to see another person, but his shaking fingers touched his lips as he looked at him. His lips and fingernails were the same pale, lead-gray color. Then his hand dropped back to his work, and he bent over the shoe again.

raw: The look and the action had occupied but an instant.
en: The look and the movement took only a second.

raw: “You have a visitor, you see,” said Monsieur Defarge.
en: "You have a visitor, you see," said Monsieur Defarge.

raw: “What did you say?”
en: "What did you say?"

raw: “Here is a visitor.”
en: "Here is a visitor."

raw: The shoemaker looked up as before, but without removing a hand from his work.
en: The shoemaker looked up as he had before, but without taking his hands off his work.

raw: “Come!” said Defarge. “Here is monsieur, who knows a well-made shoe when he sees one.
en: "Come!" said Defarge. "Here is a gentleman who knows a good shoe when he sees one.

raw: Show him that shoe you are working at.
en: Show him the shoe you are working on.

raw: Take it, monsieur.”
en: Take it, sir."

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.

raw: Lorry took it in his hand.
en: Lorry took it in his hand.

raw: “Tell monsieur what kind of shoe it is, and the maker’s name.”
en: "Tell the gentleman what kind of shoe it is, and the maker's name."

raw: There was a longer pause than usual, before the shoemaker replied:
en: There was a longer pause than usual before the shoemaker answered:

raw: “I forget what it was you asked me.
en: "I forget what you asked me.

raw: What did you say?”
en: What did you say?"

raw: “I said, couldn’t you describe the kind of shoe, for monsieur’s information?”
en: "I asked if you could describe the kind of shoe for this gentleman."

raw: “It is a lady’s shoe.
en: "It is a lady's shoe.

raw: It is a young lady’s walking-shoe.
en: It is a young lady's walking shoe.

raw: It is in the present mode.
en: It is in the latest fashion.

raw: I never saw the mode. I have had a pattern in my hand.” He glanced at the shoe with some little passing touch of pride.
en: I have never seen the fashion, but I have held the pattern in my hand." He glanced at the shoe with a small, brief hint of pride.

raw: “And the maker’s name?” said Defarge.
en: "And the maker's name?" said Defarge.

raw: Now that he had no work to hold, he laid the knuckles of the right hand in the hollow of the left, and then the knuckles of the left hand in the hollow of the right, and then passed a hand across his bearded chin, and so on in regular changes, without a moment’s intermission.
en: He had no work to hold now. So he put the knuckles of his right hand in the palm of his left. Then the knuckles of his left hand in the palm of his right. Then he rubbed his hand over his bearded chin. He kept repeating this movement without stopping.

raw: The task of recalling him from the vagrancy into which he always sank when he had spoken, was like recalling some very weak person from a swoon, or endeavouring, in the hope of some disclosure, to stay the spirit of a fast-dying man.
en: Bringing his mind back from the blank state it slid into after speaking was no easy thing. It was like trying to wake a very weak person from a deep faint. Or trying to keep a dying man alive just long enough to say one last important word.

raw: “Did you ask me for my name?”
en: "Did you ask me for my name?"

raw: “Assuredly I did.”
en: "Yes, I did."

raw: “One Hundred and Five, North Tower.”
en: "One Hundred and Five, North Tower."

raw: “Is that all?”
en: "Is that all?"

raw: “One Hundred and Five, North Tower.”
en: "One Hundred and Five, North Tower."

raw: With a weary sound that was not a sigh, nor a groan, he bent to work again, until the silence was again broken.
en: With a tired sound that was not quite a sigh or a groan, he bent back to his work, until the silence was broken again.

raw: “You are not a shoemaker by trade?” said Mr.
en: "You are not a shoemaker by trade, are you?" asked Mr.

raw: Lorry, looking steadfastly at him.
en: Lorry, looking at him closely.

raw: His haggard eyes turned to Defarge as if he would have transferred the question to him: but as no help came from that quarter, they turned back on the questioner when they had sought the ground.
en: His tired eyes turned to Defarge, as if he wanted Defarge to answer for him. But when no help came from that side, his eyes looked down at the floor, and then back up at Mr. Lorry.

raw: “I am not a shoemaker by trade?
en: "I am not a shoemaker by trade?

raw: No, I was not a shoemaker by trade.
en: No, I was not a shoemaker by trade.

raw: I-I learnt it here.
en: I, I learned it here.

raw: I taught myself.
en: I taught myself.

raw: I asked leave to--”
en: I asked permission to, "

raw: He lapsed away, even for minutes, ringing those measured changes on his hands the whole time.
en: He drifted off for several minutes, repeating the same pattern with his hands the entire time.

raw: His eyes came slowly back, at last, to the face from which they had wandered; when they rested on it, he started, and resumed, in the manner of a sleeper that moment awake, reverting to a subject of last night.
en: His eyes slowly came back to Mr. Lorry's face. When they focused on him, he started, and continued speaking like a sleeper who had just woken up and gone back to a topic from the night before.

raw: “I asked leave to teach myself, and I got it with much difficulty after a long while, and I have made shoes ever since.”
en: "I asked permission to teach myself, and I got it with great difficulty after a long time. I have made shoes ever since."

raw: As he held out his hand for the shoe that had been taken from him, Mr.
en: As he reached out his hand for the shoe, Mr.

raw: Lorry said, still looking steadfastly in his face:
en: Lorry said, still looking directly at him:

raw: “Monsieur Manette, do you remember nothing of me?”
en: "Monsieur Manette, do you remember anything about me?"

raw: The shoe dropped to the ground, and he sat looking fixedly at the questioner.
en: The shoe fell to the ground, and he sat staring intensely at the questioner.

raw: “Monsieur Manette”; Mr.
en: "Monsieur Manette," Mr.

raw: Lorry laid his hand upon Defarge’s arm; “do you remember nothing of this man?
en: Lorry said, putting his hand on Defarge's arm, "do you remember nothing of this man?

raw: Look at him.
en: Look at him.

raw: Look at me.
en: Look at me.

raw: Is there no old banker, no old business, no old servant, no old time, rising in your mind, Monsieur Manette?”
en: Is there no memory of your old banker, your old business, your old servant, or your past life coming back to your mind, Monsieur Manette?"

raw: As the captive of many years sat looking fixedly, by turns, at Mr.
en: The long-time prisoner sat looking intensely, first at Mr.

raw: Lorry and at Defarge, some long obliterated marks of an actively intent intelligence in the middle of the forehead, gradually forced themselves through the black mist that had fallen on him.
en: Lorry and then at Defarge. Some long-lost signs of intelligence and deep thought began to show on his forehead. They broke through the dark cloud that hung over his mind.

raw: They were overclouded again, they were fainter, they were gone; but they had been there.
en: The signs faded again, grew weaker, and then disappeared, but they had definitely been there. His daughter had crept along the wall to where she could see him.

raw: And so exactly was the expression repeated on the fair young face of her who had crept along the wall to a point where she could see him, and where she now stood looking at him, with hands which at first had been only raised in frightened compassion, if not even to keep him off and shut out the sight of him, but which were now extending towards him, trembling with eagerness to lay the spectral face upon her warm young breast, and love it back to life and hope--so exactly was the expression repeated (though in stronger characters) on her fair young face, that it looked as though it had passed like a moving light, from him to her.
en: She stood there looking at him. At first, her hands had been raised in frightened pity, as if to shield herself from the sight of him. But now she was reaching out to him, trembling with eagerness to hold his ghost-like face to her warm chest and love him back to life and hope. That same expression was reflected on her face, much stronger and clearer than on his. It looked as if a moving light had passed directly from him to her.

raw: Darkness had fallen on him in its place.
en: But the darkness returned and took over his mind again.

raw: He looked at the two, less and less attentively, and his eyes in gloomy abstraction sought the ground and looked about him in the old way.
en: He looked at the two men with less and less interest, and his eyes wandered down to the floor in a sad, blank stare, looking around in his usual confused way.

raw: Finally, with a deep long sigh, he took the shoe up, and resumed his work.
en: Finally, with a long, deep sigh, he picked up the shoe and went back to work.

raw: “Have you recognised him, monsieur?” asked Defarge in a whisper.
en: "Did you recognize him, sir?" Defarge asked in a whisper.

raw: “Yes; for a moment.
en: "Yes, for a moment.

raw: At first I thought it quite hopeless, but I have unquestionably seen, for a single moment, the face that I once knew so well.
en: At first I thought it was completely hopeless, but I definitely saw the face I used to know so well for a single second.

raw: Hush!
en: Shh!

raw: Let us draw further back.
en: Let's step back a little.

raw: Hush!”
en: Shh!"

raw: She had moved from the wall of the garret, very near to the bench on which he sat.
en: She had moved away from the attic wall and was now standing very close to the bench where he sat.

raw: There was something awful in his unconsciousness of the figure that could have put out its hand and touched him as he stooped over his labour.
en: It was deeply sad and unsettling that he was completely unaware of her standing right there, close enough to reach out and touch him as he bent over his work.

raw: Not a word was spoken, not a sound was made.
en: Not a word was spoken; not a sound was made.

raw: She stood, like a spirit, beside him, and he bent over his work.
en: She stood beside him like a quiet spirit, while he bent over his work.

raw: It happened, at length, that he had occasion to change the instrument in his hand, for his shoemaker’s knife.
en: Eventually, he needed to switch the tool in his hand for his shoemaker's knife.

raw: It lay on that side of him which was not the side on which she stood.
en: The knife lay on the side away from where she was standing.

raw: He had taken it up, and was stooping to work again, when his eyes caught the skirt of her dress.
en: He picked it up and was leaning down to work again when his eyes caught the edge of her dress.

raw: He raised them, and saw her face.
en: He looked up and saw her face.

raw: The two spectators started forward, but she stayed them with a motion of her hand.
en: The two men rushed forward, but she stopped them with a wave of her hand.

raw: She had no fear of his striking at her with the knife, though they had.
en: She was not afraid that he would strike her with the knife, even though the men were.

raw: He stared at her with a fearful look, and after a while his lips began to form some words, though no sound proceeded from them.
en: He stared at her with a frightened look, and after a moment, his lips began to form words, though no sound came out.

raw: By degrees, in the pauses of his quick and laboured breathing, he was heard to say:
en: Gradually, during the pauses in his fast, heavy breathing, they heard him say:

raw: “What is this?”
en: "What is this?"

raw: With the tears streaming down her face, she put her two hands to her lips, and kissed them to him; then clasped them on her breast, as if she laid his ruined head there.
en: With tears streaming down her face, she blew him a kiss with both hands, then pressed her hands to her chest, as if holding his broken head against her heart.

raw: “You are not the gaoler’s daughter?”
en: "You are not the jailer's daughter?"

raw: She sighed “No.”
en: She sighed, "No."

raw: “Who are you?”
en: "Who are you?"

raw: Not yet trusting the tones of her voice, she sat down on the bench beside him.
en: Not yet trusting herself to speak clearly, she sat down on the bench next to him.

raw: He recoiled, but she laid her hand upon his arm.
en: He pulled back, but she gently laid her hand on his arm.

raw: A strange thrill struck him when she did so, and visibly passed over his frame; he laid the knife down softly, as he sat staring at her.
en: A strange shiver ran through his entire body when she touched him. He set the knife down gently, continuing to stare at her.

raw: Her golden hair, which she wore in long curls, had been hurriedly pushed aside, and fell down over her neck.
en: Her golden hair, which she wore in long curls, had been pushed back in her excitement and fell over her neck.

raw: Advancing his hand by little and little, he took it up and looked at it.
en: Moving his hand very slowly, he reached out, picked up a lock of her hair, and looked at it.

raw: In the midst of the action he went astray, and, with another deep sigh, fell to work at his shoemaking.
en: But while doing this, his mind drifted away again, and with another deep sigh, he went back to making shoes.

raw: But not for long.
en: But not for long.

raw: Releasing his arm, she laid her hand upon his shoulder.
en: Freeing her arm, she laid her hand on his shoulder.

raw: After looking doubtfully at it, two or three times, as if to be sure that it was really there, he laid down his work, put his hand to his neck, and took off a blackened string with a scrap of folded rag attached to it.
en: He looked at her hand doubtfully two or three times, as if to make sure it was really there. Then he laid down his work, reached for his neck, and pulled off a blackened string with a small piece of folded rag tied to it.

raw: He opened this, carefully, on his knee, and it contained a very little quantity of hair: not more than one or two long golden hairs, which he had, in some old day, wound off upon his finger.
en: He carefully opened the rag on his knee. Inside was a tiny bit of hair, only one or two long golden strands that he had wound around his finger a long time ago.

raw: He took her hair into his hand again, and looked closely at it. “It is the same.
en: He took her hair in his hand again and looked closely at it. "It is the same.

raw: How can it be!
en: How can it be!

raw: When was it!
en: When was this?

raw: How was it!”
en: How did this happen?"

raw: As the concentrated expression returned to his forehead, he seemed to become conscious that it was in hers too.
en: As the deep, focused look returned to his forehead, he seemed to notice that she had the exact same expression.

raw: He turned her full to the light, and looked at her.
en: He turned her face directly toward the light and looked at her.

raw: “She had laid her head upon my shoulder, that night when I was summoned out--she had a fear of my going, though I had none--and when I was brought to the North Tower they found these upon my sleeve. ‘You will leave me them?
en: "She laid her head on my shoulder the night I was called away. She was afraid of my leaving, though I was not. And when I was brought to the North Tower, they found these strands of hair on my sleeve. 'Will you let me keep them?

raw: They can never help me to escape in the body, though they may in the spirit.’ Those were the words I said.
en: They can never help my body escape, but they might help my soul.' Those were the words I said.

raw: I remember them very well.”
en: I remember them very well."

raw: He formed this speech with his lips many times before he could utter it.
en: He shaped these words with his lips many times before he could say them out loud.

raw: But when he did find spoken words for it, they came to him coherently, though slowly.
en: But when he finally spoke, his words made sense, even though they came slowly.

raw: “How was this?--_Was it you_?”
en: "How could this be? ,  _Was it you_?"

raw: Once more, the two spectators started, as he turned upon her with a frightful suddenness.
en: Once again, the two men jumped in surprise as he turned to her with terrifying suddenness.

raw: But she sat perfectly still in his grasp, and only said, in a low voice, “I entreat you, good gentlemen, do not come near us, do not speak, do not move!”
en: But she sat completely still in his grip. In a quiet voice she said, "I beg you, gentlemen, do not come near us, do not speak, and do not move!"

raw: “Hark!” he exclaimed. “Whose voice was that?”
en: "Listen!" he cried. "Whose voice was that?"

raw: His hands released her as he uttered this cry, and went up to his white hair, which they tore in a frenzy.
en: His hands let go of her as he shouted, reaching up to his white hair and pulling at it wildly.

raw: It died out, as everything but his shoemaking did die out of him, and he refolded his little packet and tried to secure it in his breast; but he still looked at her, and gloomily shook his head.
en: But the outburst soon faded, just as everything except his shoemaking always faded from his mind. He folded his little rag packet back up and tried to hide it in his shirt, but he kept looking at her, shaking his head sadly.

raw: “No, no, no; you are too young, too blooming.
en: "No, no, no. You are too young, too full of life.

raw: It can’t be.
en: It cannot be.

raw: See what the prisoner is.
en: Look at what a prisoner I am.

raw: These are not the hands she knew, this is not the face she knew, this is not a voice she ever heard.
en: These are not the hands she knew, this is not the face she knew, and this is not a voice she ever heard.

raw: No, no.
en: No, no.

raw: She was--and He was--before the slow years of the North Tower--ages ago.
en: She and I existed before the long, slow years in the North Tower, ages ago.

raw: What is your name, my gentle angel?”
en: What is your name, my gentle angel?"

raw: Hailing his softened tone and manner, his daughter fell upon her knees before him, with her appealing hands upon his breast.
en: Grateful for his softer tone and gentle manner, his daughter knelt in front of him, placing her pleading hands on his chest.

raw: “O, sir, at another time you shall know my name, and who my mother was, and who my father, and how I never knew their hard, hard history.
en: "Oh, sir, at another time you will know my name, and who my mother and father were, and why I never knew their sad history.

raw: But I cannot tell you at this time, and I cannot tell you here.
en: But I cannot tell you now, and I cannot tell you here.

raw: All that I may tell you, here and now, is, that I pray to you to touch me and to bless me.
en: All I can tell you right here and now is that I beg you to touch me and bless me.

raw: Kiss me, kiss me!
en: Kiss me, kiss me!

raw: O my dear, my dear!”
en: Oh, my dear, my dear father!"

raw: His cold white head mingled with her radiant hair, which warmed and lighted it as though it were the light of Freedom shining on him.
en: His cold white head rested against her bright, golden hair, which seemed to warm and light it up as if the light of freedom itself were shining on him.

raw: “If you hear in my voice--I don’t know that it is so, but I hope it is--if you hear in my voice any resemblance to a voice that once was sweet music in your ears, weep for it, weep for it!
en: "If you hear in my voice, I do not know if it is true, but I hope it is, any sound that reminds you of a voice that was once sweet music to your ears, cry for it, cry for it!

raw: If you touch, in touching my hair, anything that recalls a beloved head that lay on your breast when you were young and free, weep for it, weep for it!
en: If, in touching my hair, you feel anything that reminds you of a beloved head that lay on your chest when you were young and free, cry for it, cry for it!

raw: If, when I hint to you of a Home that is before us, where I will be true to you with all my duty and with all my faithful service, I bring back the remembrance of a Home long desolate, while your poor heart pined away, weep for it, weep for it!”
en: If, when I talk about the home waiting for us, where I will care for you with all my duty and faithful love, I bring back the memory of a home that was empty for so long while your poor heart suffered, cry for it, cry for it!"

raw: She held him closer round the neck, and rocked him on her breast like a child.
en: She held him tighter around the neck, rocking him against her chest like a child.

raw: “If, when I tell you, dearest dear, that your agony is over, and that I have come here to take you from it, and that we go to England to be at peace and at rest, I cause you to think of your useful life laid waste, and of our native France so wicked to you, weep for it, weep for it!
en: "If, when I tell you, my dearest, that your suffering is over, and that I have come to take you away from this place to England where we can live in peace and rest, I make you think of your wasted life and how cruel our native France has been to you, cry for it, cry for it!

raw: And if, when I shall tell you of my name, and of my father who is living, and of my mother who is dead, you learn that I have to kneel to my honoured father, and implore his pardon for having never for his sake striven all day and lain awake and wept all night, because the love of my poor mother hid his torture from me, weep for it, weep for it!
en: And if, when I tell you my name and about my father who is alive and my mother who is dead, you learn that I must kneel to my honored father and beg his forgiveness for never working all day, staying awake, and crying all night for his sake, because my mother's love kept his suffering a secret from me, cry for it, cry for it!

raw: Weep for her, then, and for me!
en: Cry for her, then, and for me!

raw: Good gentlemen, thank God!
en: Gentlemen, thank God!

raw: I feel his sacred tears upon my face, and his sobs strike against my heart.
en: I feel his tears on my face, and his sobs touch my heart.

raw: O, see!
en: Oh, look!

raw: Thank God for us, thank God!”
en: Thank God for us, thank God!"

raw: He had sunk in her arms, and his face dropped on her breast: a sight so touching, yet so terrible in the tremendous wrong and suffering which had gone before it, that the two beholders covered their faces.
en: He sank into her arms, and his face fell against her chest. It was a sight so touching, yet so terrible because of the great pain and injustice that had caused it, that the two men watching covered their faces.

raw: When the quiet of the garret had been long undisturbed, and his heaving breast and shaken form had long yielded to the calm that must follow all storms--emblem to humanity, of the rest and silence into which the storm called Life must hush at last--they came forward to raise the father and daughter from the ground.
en: The attic room had been quiet for a long time. His heavy breathing slowed. His trembling body finally calmed down. As always, the storm had ended in quiet peace. The two men came forward to help the father and daughter up.

raw: He had gradually dropped to the floor, and lay there in a lethargy, worn out.
en: He had slowly slipped to the floor and lay there in a deep, exhausted sleep.

raw: She had nestled down with him, that his head might lie upon her arm; and her hair drooping over him curtained him from the light.
en: She had huddled down with him so that his head rested on her arm, and her long hair fell over him like a curtain to block out the light.

en: "If we can do it without waking him," she whispered, raising her hand to Mr.

en: Lorry as he stood over them, blowing his nose repeatedly, "could we arrange to leave Paris immediately? That way, we can take him directly from this door to the carriage."

raw: “But, consider.
en: "But think about it.

raw: Is he fit for the journey?” asked Mr.
en: Is he strong enough to travel?" asked Mr.

raw: Lorry.
en: Lorry.

raw: “More fit for that, I think, than to remain in this city, so dreadful to him.”
en: "He is much readier for that, I think, than to stay in this city that has been so terrible to him."

raw: “It is true,” said Defarge, who was kneeling to look on and hear. “More than that; Monsieur Manette is, for all reasons, best out of France.
en: "That is true," said Defarge, who had knelt down to watch and listen. "In fact, Monsieur Manette is much better off leaving France entirely.

raw: Say, shall I hire a carriage and post-horses?”
en: Should I go hire a carriage and fresh horses?"

raw: “That’s business,” said Mr.
en: "That is a matter of business," said Mr.

raw: Lorry, resuming on the shortest notice his methodical manners; “and if business is to be done, I had better do it.”
en: Lorry, quickly returning to his organized, professional way of speaking. "And if business needs to be done, I had better take care of it."

raw: “Then be so kind,” urged Miss Manette, “as to leave us here.
en: Miss Manette urged, "Then please, leave us here for now.

raw: You see how composed he has become, and you cannot be afraid to leave him with me now.
en: You see how calm he is, and you don't need to worry about leaving him with me.

raw: Why should you be?
en: Why would you be?

raw: If you will lock the door to secure us from interruption, I do not doubt that you will find him, when you come back, as quiet as you leave him.
en: If you lock the door to make sure no one interrupts us, I am sure you will find him just as quiet when you return.

raw: In any case, I will take care of him until you return, and then we will remove him straight.”
en: I will watch over him until you get back, and then we can move him immediately."

en: Both Mr.

raw: Lorry and Defarge were rather disinclined to this course, and in favour of one of them remaining.
en: Lorry and Defarge were reluctant to do this and preferred to have one of them stay behind.

raw: But, as there were not only carriage and horses to be seen to, but travelling papers; and as time pressed, for the day was drawing to an end, it came at last to their hastily dividing the business that was necessary to be done, and hurrying away to do it.
en: They had to arrange for the carriage, horses, and travel papers. Time was running out as the day ended. So they split up the tasks and hurried off to complete them.

raw: Then, as the darkness closed in, the daughter laid her head down on the hard ground close at the father’s side, and watched him.
en: Then, as darkness filled the room, the daughter laid her head on the hard floor right next to her father and watched him.

raw: The darkness deepened and deepened, and they both lay quiet, until a light gleamed through the chinks in the wall.
en: The darkness grew deeper and deeper, and they both lay quietly until a light shone through the cracks in the wall.

en: Lorry and Monsieur Defarge had prepared everything for the trip. They brought traveling coats, blankets, bread, meat, wine, and hot coffee.

raw: Monsieur Defarge put this provender, and the lamp he carried, on the shoemaker’s bench (there was nothing else in the garret but a pallet bed), and he and Mr.
en: Monsieur Defarge placed the food and the lamp he was carrying on the shoemaker's workbench, the only other thing in the room being a simple straw bed.

raw: Lorry roused the captive, and assisted him to his feet.
en: Then he and Mr. Lorry woke the prisoner and helped him stand up.

raw: No human intelligence could have read the mysteries of his mind, in the scared blank wonder of his face.
en: No one could have understood what was going on in his mind by looking at the scared, blank look on his face.

raw: Whether he knew what had happened, whether he recollected what they had said to him, whether he knew that he was free, were questions which no sagacity could have solved.
en: Whether he understood what had happened, remembered what they had said, or even knew he was free were questions that no one could answer.

raw: They tried speaking to him; but, he was so confused, and so very slow to answer, that they took fright at his bewilderment, and agreed for the time to tamper with him no more.
en: They tried talking to him, but he was so confused and slow to respond that they became worried by his state and decided to leave him alone for the time being.

raw: He had a wild, lost manner of occasionally clasping his head in his hands, that had not been seen in him before; yet, he had some pleasure in the mere sound of his daughter’s voice, and invariably turned to it when she spoke.
en: He had a wild, lost way of holding his head in his hands sometimes, which they had not seen before. Yet, he seemed to find some comfort in the sound of his daughter's voice, and always turned toward her whenever she spoke.

raw: In the submissive way of one long accustomed to obey under coercion, he ate and drank what they gave him to eat and drink, and put on the cloak and other wrappings, that they gave him to wear.
en: With the obedient attitude of someone long forced to follow orders, he ate and drank whatever they offered, and put on the coat and blankets they gave him.

raw: He readily responded to his daughter’s drawing her arm through his, and took--and kept--her hand in both his own.
en: He willingly let his daughter put her arm through his, and took, and held, her hand in both of his.

raw: They began to descend; Monsieur Defarge going first with the lamp, Mr.
en: They began to walk down the stairs, with Monsieur Defarge leading the way with the lamp and Mr.

raw: Lorry closing the little procession.
en: Lorry walking at the end.

raw: They had not traversed many steps of the long main staircase when he stopped, and stared at the roof and round at the walls.
en: They had only gone down a few steps of the long main staircase when the doctor stopped, staring up at the ceiling and around at the walls.

raw: “You remember the place, my father?
en: "Do you remember this place, father?

raw: You remember coming up here?”
en: Do you remember coming up here?"

raw: “What did you say?”
en: "What did you say?"

raw: But, before she could repeat the question, he murmured an answer as if she had repeated it.
en: But before she could repeat the question, he muttered an answer as if she had already done so.

raw: “Remember?
en: "Remember?

raw: No, I don’t remember.
en: No, I don't remember.

raw: It was so very long ago.”
en: It was so very long ago."

raw: That he had no recollection whatever of his having been brought from his prison to that house, was apparent to them.
en: It was clear that he had no memory of being brought from the prison to this house.

raw: They heard him mutter, “One Hundred and Five, North Tower;” and when he looked about him, it evidently was for the strong fortress-walls which had long encompassed him.
en: They heard him mutter, "One Hundred and Five, North Tower." When he looked around, he was clearly looking for the thick fortress walls that had surrounded him for so long.

raw: On their reaching the courtyard he instinctively altered his tread, as being in expectation of a drawbridge; and when there was no drawbridge, and he saw the carriage waiting in the open street, he dropped his daughter’s hand and clasped his head again.
en: When they reached the courtyard, he automatically changed his step, expecting to cross a drawbridge. When there was no drawbridge and he saw the carriage waiting in the open street, he let go of his daughter's hand and held his head in his hands again.

raw: No crowd was about the door; no people were discernible at any of the many windows; not even a chance passerby was in the street.
en: There was no crowd outside the door. No one looked out from the many windows. Not even a single person walked down the street.

raw: An unnatural silence and desertion reigned there.
en: An unnatural silence and emptiness filled the air.

raw: Only one soul was to be seen, and that was Madame Defarge--who leaned against the door-post, knitting, and saw nothing.
en: Only one person was visible. That was Madame Defarge. She leaned against the doorframe, knitting, and appearing to see nothing.

raw: The prisoner had got into a coach, and his daughter had followed him, when Mr.
en: The prisoner climbed into the carriage and his daughter followed him. But just as Mr.

raw: Lorry’s feet were arrested on the step by his asking, miserably, for his shoemaking tools and the unfinished shoes.
en: Lorry was stepping in, he stopped on the step because the doctor began pleading sadly for his shoemaking tools and the unfinished shoes.

raw: Madame Defarge immediately called to her husband that she would get them, and went, knitting, out of the lamplight, through the courtyard.
en: Madame Defarge immediately called out to her husband that she would get them, and walked out of the lamplight, knitting, across the courtyard.

raw: She quickly brought them down and handed them in;--and immediately afterwards leaned against the door-post, knitting, and saw nothing.
en: She returned quickly and handed the tools into the carriage. Then she went straight back to the doorframe, leaned against it, and went on knitting, appearing to see nothing.

raw: Defarge got upon the box, and gave the word “To the Barrier!” The postilion cracked his whip, and they clattered away under the feeble over-swinging lamps.
en: Defarge climbed onto the driver's seat and shouted, "To the city gate!" The driver cracked his whip, and the carriage clattered away under the dim, hanging streetlamps.

raw: Under the over-swinging lamps--swinging ever brighter in the better streets, and ever dimmer in the worse--and by lighted shops, gay crowds, illuminated coffee-houses, and theatre-doors, to one of the city gates.
en: They rode under the hanging streetlamps. The lamps swung brighter in the wealthier streets and dimmer in the poorer ones. They passed lit-up shops, happy crowds, bright cafes, and theater entrances on their way to one of the city gates.

raw: Soldiers with lanterns, at the guard-house there. “Your papers, travellers!” “See here then, Monsieur the Officer,” said Defarge, getting down, and taking him gravely apart, “these are the papers of monsieur inside, with the white head.
en: Soldiers with lanterns stood at the guardhouse there. "Your papers, travelers!" one called out. "Look here, officer," said Defarge, getting down and pulling him aside. "These are the papers of the gentleman inside with the white hair.

raw: They were consigned to me, with him, at the--” He dropped his voice, there was a flutter among the military lanterns, and one of them being handed into the coach by an arm in uniform, the eyes connected with the arm looked, not an every day or an every night look, at monsieur with the white head. “It is well.
en: He was placed in my care at the, " He lowered his voice, and there was a stir among the soldiers' lanterns. A uniformed arm reached into the carriage with a light, and the eyes behind the arm stared with a look of deep surprise and curiosity at the white-haired man. "Everything is in order.

raw: Forward!” from the uniform. “Adieu!” from Defarge.
en: Move along!" said the soldier. "Goodbye!" replied Defarge.

raw: And so, under a short grove of feebler and feebler over-swinging lamps, out under the great grove of stars.
en: And so, they drove under a few last, dim hanging lamps, and out under the vast sky of stars.

raw: Beneath that arch of unmoved and eternal lights; some, so remote from this little earth that the learned tell us it is doubtful whether their rays have even yet discovered it, as a point in space where anything is suffered or done: the shadows of the night were broad and black.
en: Above them stretched a canopy of quiet, eternal stars. Some are so far away that scientists say their light may not have even reached our small Earth yet, not enough to show a place where people suffer and live. Beneath that canopy, the shadows of the night were wide and dark.

en: All through the cold, restless hours of the night until dawn, the same question whispered in the mind of Mr.

en: Jarvis Lorry. He sat opposite the man who had been dug out of his living grave, wondering what parts of his mind were lost forever and what could still be healed:

en: "I hope you care to be recalled to life?"

en: And the old answer:

en: "I can't say."
